summary: Negative provisional balance and missing reserved credits after dedicated failover and cross-region proration
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightArc Health reports a negative provisional balance on their monthly bill after an automated dedicated failover between us-west and us-east. Reserved capacity credits that should have applied to the failover window are missing, and the invoice shows a -$1,240 provisional line item that the customer can't reconcile.

Impact: Customer-facing invoice variance for a healthcare customer (enterprise, dedicated) with potential chargeback to internal cost center. Customer is asking for an expedited reconciliation and provisional credit while we investigate.

Environment: Dedicated pool assigned to BrightArc Health, primary region us-west, failover triggered to us-east during scheduled maintenance window (2026-03-06 23:50 UTC). Billing window is hourly-based with proration.

Expected behavior: Reserved-hours proration should allocate hours across regions without creating negative provisional balances. Postbacks from edge proxies should be attributed to the correct hourly bucket and carry reserved credits applied at the reserved rate.

Actual behavior: After failover the hourly postback reordering and a cross-region proration step appear to have double-counted a partial refund and removed the reserved-hour credit for the failover window, resulting in a negative provisional balance.

Customer request: Immediate provisional credit so final invoice does not block autopay and a postmortem explaining root cause and guardrails put in place.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate dedicated pool failover: drain us-west node and failover requests to us-east during an hourly boundary (e.g., 23:50 UTC).
Trigger a mix of streaming and non-streaming requests that would consume reserved capacity and warm KV cache (small chat workload).
Allow postback processor to receive delayed edge postbacks (simulate 2-6 minute lag).
Run hourly proration/reconciliation job against the postback set and observe allocation of reserved credits and provisional line items.

investigation_notes: 03/10 09:30 - Initial triage: billing reconciler shows zero allocated_reserved_hours for the affected window while usage shows reserved queue consumption. Hypothesis: postbacks from us-west were replayed and attributed after proration ran, causing reserved-credit to be overwritten.

03/10 12:05 - SRE (Ben Carter) reproduced scenario in staging by injecting delayed postbacks; observed last-writer-wins policy causes proration job to re-evaluate window and drop earlier reserved allocation when out-of-order events arrive.

03/11 15:22 - Found race between ded-provisioning update (marks reserved hours consumed) and proration reconciler (applies credits). If proration completes while edge postbacks are still arriving, subsequent late postbacks trigger a correction flow that can create a negative provisional balance when combined with an earlier refund event.
03/11 17:40 - Confirmed edge-proxy metric spikes during the maintenance window (packet drops and retries). Postback_count and requeue logs indicate multiple delayed batches for this tenant.
comments: Aisha Kumar (Support) 2026-03-10: Reached out to customer, they attached a PDF of the provisional invoice showing -$1,240. Customer asks for provisional credit and ETA for fix. Raised priority to P1.

Ben Carter (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with delayed postbacks. Suspect race between proration job and late postbacks; paging billing owner. Added SUP-30192 to track cross-tenant proration hardening.

Lina Morales (Billing) 2026-03-11: Noted proration service uses last-writer-wins on overlapping windows, which can drop reserved-hour allocations if late events include a refund delta. Filing internal task to add idempotency markers and watermarking for postbacks. See linked PR for a proposed guard: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4213

BrightArc Finance (customer) 2026-03-11: Thank you. Please confirm provisional credit and whether this will affect final invoiced amount. We need assurance for our cost center reconciliation by EOD 2026-03-12.
Ben Carter (SRE) 2026-03-12: Applied provisional credit of $1,240 to tenant as an immediate workaround (internal memo ref: billing-wo-2026-03-12). Continuing work on permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround applied: provisional credit of $1,240 applied to BrightArc Health's account to prevent autopay failure. Technical fix: update proration reconciler to use stable watermarks for postback attribution and add idempotent reserved-hour markers so late-arriving postbacks cannot produce negative provisional balances. Deployment plan: patch proration service and postback-processor in staging (PR #4213), run 72-hour canary with synthetic delayed-postback workload, then roll to prod during low-traffic window. Follow-up: postmortem to be published to Confluence and customer-facing summary to be sent by CS.
follow_up_actions: Patch proration reconciler to use watermarking and idempotency markers (owner: billing team, ETA 2026-03-18).
Add integration test that simulates delayed postbacks across hourly boundary (owner: SRE, ETA 2026-03-15).
Publish customer-facing postmortem and send to BrightArc Finance explaining credit and timeline (owner: CS, ETA 2026-03-13).
